title: Financial Sector Update

claims.reason: The endorsed no-increase interpretation is too strong. Recipient-level study finds employment rose 6.8 percentage points after early withdrawal, while benefit loss was much larger than earnings recovery. A shortage can persist despite a positive effect.

evidence.title: Early withdrawal of pandemic unemployment insurance
evidence.publisher: Coombs et al, AEA Papers and Proceedings
evidence.finding: Bank-transaction difference-in-differences study of 16,253 recipients: benefit receipt declined 36.3 percentage points, employment rose 6.8 pp by early September; cumulative benefits fell $2,529, earnings rose $292. Ending aid did increase employment but did not replace lost income broadly.

evidence.title: CPI misconceptions
evidence.finding: BLS rejects large constant adjustments attributed to methodological changes. Geometric means reduced annual growth less than 0.3 percentage points; the pre-1983 housing asset approach can yield lower inflation when housing prices fall. No 2021 old-method reconstruction is provided.

claims.next_check: Reconstruct 1980 housing/interest-cost weights and formulas using 2021 data; do not substitute an unexplained constant adjustment.

framework_lessons: Separate credit safety from duration and funding risk.
assessment: Persistent inflation and rent pressure were useful calls. Sberbank exposed the difference between cheap fundamentals and investable foreign-holder rights; DBS and CNQ fared well. Treasury-heavy bank portfolios were incorrectly treated as broadly safe. Crypto analysis correctly identified correlation and legal distinctions, but sometimes converted complex securities, governance and tax questions into overly categorical claims.
